Grade: Grade 2
Subject: HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: USE AND CARE OF 2.0 PERSONAL HYGIENE
Subject: HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Use and care of 2.0 Personal Hygiene helps you succeed in HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: USE AND CARE OF 2.0 PERSONAL HYGIENE
Use and care of 2.0 Personal Hygiene is part of Science learning. Connect every idea to something you can observe.
Use safe examples only. Do not try dangerous experiments without a teacher.
Write definitions in your own words, then add one drawing or real-life example.

PART 1: Identify the items used for  In groups, provide

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the items used for  In groups, provide. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the items used for  In groups, provide.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Use and care of 2.0 Personal Hygiene” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the items used for  In groups, provide. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the importance of not be shared caring for personal items to 

What this means
In this part you learn to Appreciate the importance of not be shared caring for personal items to . You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Appreciate the importance of not be shared caring for personal items to .
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Use and care of 2.0 Personal Hygiene matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Appreciate the importance of not be shared caring for personal items to . Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Use and care of 2.0 Personal Hygiene is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Use and care of 2.0 Personal Hygiene” around your school. (skill: identify the items used for  In groups, provide)

Example 2: Say why Use and care of 2.0 Personal Hygiene matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: Appreciate the importance of not be shared caring for personal items to )

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Use and care of 2.0 Personal Hygiene to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the items used for  In groups, provide.
3. Practise this skill: Appreciate the importance of not be shared caring for personal items to .
4. Make one local Kenya example of Use and care of 2.0 Personal Hygiene from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Use and care of 2.0 Personal Hygiene: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Use and care of 2.0 Personal Hygiene?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we clean b) give reasons why we should not (examples: combs, toothbrush, face personal items?
2. Why should we not towel, handkerchief, socks and shoes, c) state the procedure used when share personal items?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Use and care of 2.0 Personal Hygiene means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the items used for  In groups, provide.
5. Be able to: Appreciate the importance of not be shared caring for personal items to .

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
